summary: thiscall factory that allocates a 548-byte object via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, default-initializes its fields (zeroing several leading dwords/bytes, storing a -1 sentinel at offset 532), stores the resulting pointer into *this (or 0 on allocation failure), and returns this. Callers span resource cleanup, file enumeration, profile loading, and texture scanning, suggesting a per-resource state struct, but the struct identity is not established.

local_names.v2: newly allocated 548-byte object (null on allocation failure)

operations.description: Call OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper with size 548; the returned pointer (v2) is the new object or null on allocation failure.
Guard on v2: when non-null the new object is default-initialized; when null the out-pointer *this is cleared instead.
Zero the leading fields of the new object: dwords at offsets 0, 4, 8, 12 and the byte at offset 16.
Zero the dword at offset 528 and store -1 into the dword at offset 532 (sentinel/default value).
Zero the byte at offset 536 and the dwords at offsets 540 and 544; re-zero the byte at offset 16 (duplicate write preserved from the raw source).
Store v2 into *this on the success path, or 0 into *this on the allocation-failure path.

Semantics of the zero-initialized fields (offsets 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 528, 536, 540, 544) and the -1 sentinel at offset 532 are unknown without a live struct probe.
The duplicate byte-zero write at offset 16 is preserved from the raw source and may indicate separate boolean fields sharing the byte.
